A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 17-page versions of the same work, with matching sections and Appendices A-C. Text extraction and visual comparison support reliable assessment of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original up-axis experiments on ShapeNet and ModelNet40, full-orientation experiments on ShapeNet, and diagnostic and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, including Tables 1 and 2, the rotation-discontinuity analysis, and qualitative ShapeNet and Objaverse results.

M1.justification: The quotient orienter, octahedral flipper, training objectives, test-time augmentation, and adaptive prediction sets are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both retain ShapeNet training and evaluation, ModelNet40 generalization testing, and qualitative Objaverse evaluation. Up-axis and full-orientation task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Upright-Net as the up-axis comparator. Table 2 retains Upright-Net-Random and Upright-Net-Oracle for full-orientation estimation, with identical comparator definitions.

E3.justification: The ShapeNet 90/10 split, point sampling, training budgets, 10-degree accuracy criterion, Chamfer-distance evaluation, and adaptive prediction set settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the with/without-TTA comparisons, prediction-set-size analysis in Figure 8, rotation-discontinuity experiment in Appendix B.4, and qualitative examples in Appendix C.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains identical mean-and-± reporting. There are no changes to run-count or seed disclosures, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains TTA accuracies of 89.2% on ShapeNet and 77.7% on ModelNet40. Pages 6-17, containing the results and appendices, are visually identical.

T1.justification: Propositions 3.1-3.3 and the definitions, derivations, and proofs in Appendix A are unchanged. Mathematical passages crossing different page boundaries are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about symmetry-robust orientation estimation, up-axis performance, full-orientation recovery, and adaptive prediction sets. The existing code-release claim merely gains an address.

C2.justification: The explanations of symmetry-related ambiguity, localized orienter failures, and the flipper's weaker generalization remain unchanged, as do the qualifications concerning Objaverse evaluation and plausible alternative orientations.

D1.justification: v3 announces release of code and model weights without a repository address. v4 adds that address in Introduction footnote 1, supplying concrete access information. Appendix B's implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. The new project address does not introduce a scholarly reference or revise a novelty claim.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are limited to the repository footnote and updated arXiv version/date stamp. The prose, terminology, and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added footnote causes local column and page reflow on pages 2-5, including shifts in existing figure placement. Figure and table content, captions, and structure remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies a concrete repository address for the code and model weights already announced in v3, modestly improving access information and reproducibility documentation. The scientific content, supporting evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
